title: DeploymentDefinition
description: Deployment descriptor for a SoftwareSupportPackage. The 'type' field says what kind of artifact is deployed (helm, docker or opennebula) and selects the 'properties' sub-schema. It does not choose the executor: the deploy order's relationship does. Describes WHAT is deployed (artifact coordinates and provider value overrides) — never WHERE or under WHICH NAME: the release identity (namespace, deploymentName) is per-deployment data and is carried by the InstalledSoftware created from the ResourceOrder.

type.description: Deployment backend type. Determines which 'properties' sub-schema applies.

version.description: Schema version of this deployment definition.

properties.description: Backend-specific deployment parameters. Shape depends on 'type'.

values.description: YAML string of provider DEFAULTS — overridable. Applied by the BPO on top of the chart's own values.yaml and below everything the consumer sets, so a consumer may change any key declared here. Use it to ship sane defaults for values the provider does not control, typically when packaging an upstream chart that cannot be forked.

enforcedValues.description: YAML string of provider LOCKS — not overridable. Applied last, after every consumer value and after any Blueprint wiring, so a key declared here cannot be changed by anyone. Use it for what must hold for the product to be the product that was sold: the image tag an offering is priced on, a security setting, a topology the support contract assumes. An order that sets a locked key is rejected, never silently clamped. Locks are per leaf: locking resources.limits.memory leaves resources.limits.cpu free. The docker branch has no equivalent yet because it has no defaults channel either — both are a deliberate follow-up.

composeFile.description: Inline docker-compose YAML content. Used when artifactType is DockerCompose.

envFile.description: Path or inline content of environment variables file.

backend.title: Backend
backend.description: What OpenNebula creates: a VM from an approved VM template (vm), an LXC system container from an approved template (lxc), a Kubernetes cluster (oneks) or a multi-VM service from an approved OneFlow service template (oneflow). A Helm application goes on a OneKS cluster in a separate order.

templateId.title: VM template
templateId.description: ID of the approved OpenNebula VM template. Required for vm and lxc. For lxc the template must declare HYPERVISOR="lxc" or none.

serviceTemplateId.title: OneFlow service template
serviceTemplateId.description: ID of the approved OneFlow service template. Required for oneflow.

kubernetesVersion.title: Kubernetes version
kubernetesVersion.description: Kubernetes version of the OneKS cluster, for example v1.34.2. Required for oneks.

flavour.title: Control plane
flavour.description: OneKS control plane: one node (standalone) or three nodes (ha). Only for oneks.

description.title: Cluster description
description.description: Free text shown with the OneKS cluster in OpenNebula. Only for oneks.

workers.title: Worker nodes
workers.description: Number of worker nodes. A new OneKS cluster starts with its control plane only, so this applies to an update, which scales the node group of the running cluster to this number. If the cluster has no node group and this number isn't 0, the update creates one with this number of nodes. The consumer sets it with the opennebulaOverride characteristic. Here it is the provider's value, which an update uses when the order sets none, and enforcedValues can lock it. Only for oneks.

nodeGroup.title: Node group
nodeGroup.description: Name of the node group an update scales. Required when the cluster has more than one node group. If the cluster has node groups and none has this name, the update is refused. If the cluster has no node group, the update creates one with this name, or "workers" when this field isn't set. The consumer can also set it with the opennebulaOverride characteristic. Only for oneks.

workerFlavour.title: Worker flavour
workerFlavour.description: OneKS flavour of the node group that an update creates when the cluster has no node group. Only for oneks.

persistent.title: Persistent disks
persistent.description: Instantiate with persistent copies of the template images, so they survive the VM or container. Only for vm and lxc.

servicePort.title: Service port
servicePort.description: Port the application listens on. The BPO publishes it with each address in the TMF638 Service, only when the product declares a ServiceSpecification. For lxc with a healthCheck, the BPO publishes the port, protocol and path of the health check instead. For vm, lxc and oneflow.

context.title: Context variables
context.description: OpenNebula CONTEXT variables for the container, with upper-case names and string values. Only for lxc.

healthCheck.title: Health check
healthCheck.description: HTTP check the BPO runs on each LXC container before it reports the deployment as running. Only for lxc.

port.title: Port
port.description: Port of the check. Defaults to servicePort, or 80.

restartMarkerPath.title: Restart marker path
restartMarkerPath.description: Path that changes after a restart, so the BPO can confirm one.

timeoutSeconds.title: Timeout
timeoutSeconds.description: Longest time, in seconds and up to one hour, that the BPO waits for the resource to be ready where it waits for it: the LXC health check, a RUNNING OneKS cluster, and the addresses of VMs and OneFlow services. For lxc it is one budget for the whole deployment, which covers the creation of the containers, the wait for RUNNING and the health check. For all backends.

enforcedValues.title: Provider locks
enforcedValues.description: Fields of this branch that the provider locks, as an object, for example {"templateId": 237}. The BPO applies them last for every backend, so no order can change them. Locks are per leaf: in an object field such as context or healthCheck, an order can't change the locked keys but can add other keys. An order that sets a locked field to another value is rejected, never silently changed.
